what: User-owned personal context layer for consumers: preferences, history, relationships and taste owned by the individual and open to any AI agent/product, instead of being re-explained to every new AI tool. Enterprises have this; individuals do not.
why_us: High-signal demand as AI agents proliferate. Privacy-preserving personal data ownership is a recurring pain (anti-cloud/offline trends). Clear willingness from builders and users.
revenue: Potential high ARPU SaaS or protocol for AI personalization layer

what: Universal cross-platform AirDrop-like file/photo sharing that works seamlessly between all devices/OS without keeping apps open on both sides.
why_us: Persistent friction in everyday file transfer. High engagement indicates broad annoyance. Opportunity for simple, reliable local/network tool.

what: Marc Lou reported $107,142 revenue in October 2026 across 16 indie products (TrustMRR $42.5k, DataFast $31k, Ship or Die $19k, etc.), 0 employees, 90% margins.
why_us: Concrete proof of multi-product indie SaaS portfolio viability with AI-assisted building. High visibility in builder community.
revenue: $107k in October, ~$40-50k+ MRR run-rate across portfolio

what: Jacky Chou crossed $100k MRR purely from software products (not courses/communities/services), stealth mode, enabled by AI.
why_us: Demonstrates pure software revenue scale for solo/small operators using modern AI tooling.

what: Nectarlink: all-in-one open-source alternative to KDE Connect / Phone Link / LocalSend for cross-device features. Grew to 4,000+ users and ~450 GitHub stars shortly after public launch; built to solve personal multi-app juggling pain.
why_us: Classic 'built for myself, others want it' micro-tool with rapid organic growth. Shows demand for unified local connectivity utilities.
revenue: Open source with potential commercial/self-hosted tiers

what: Persistent demand for offline-first, privacy-focused, local-only tools (anti-subscription/cloud fatigue). From large HN analysis of 12k+ 'I wish' posts: people still asking for tools that were launched years ago but remain incomplete or too cloud/subscription-heavy.
why_us: High-volume recurring signal across years. 7%+ of requests specifically privacy/offline. Strong monetization potential via one-time or local licenses.

what: Better SaaS spend management and visibility: tools to combat SaaS sprawl, overlapping subscriptions, unpredictable costs, and poor attribution of spend. Multiple G2/Capterra signals of expensive, incomplete existing solutions.
why_us: Businesses overspend on software; high willingness to pay for clarity and savings. Recurring enterprise/SMB pain.
engagement: Multiple review mentions of expense and missing features

what: Website-to-native-app conversion tool (web to APK/iOS). High search volume (~9.9k/mo for related terms), low competition, solves SMB pain of lacking resources for mobile apps.
why_us: Validated demand via search data. AI makes conversion feasible. Clear path to $5-15k MRR micro-SaaS.

what: AI agent security layer (e.g. Wormhole-style): pre-signature checks for recipient/amount/chain vs quote, hidden instruction detection, spending limits, kill switch for agents handling real money. Hosted checks at $0.003 with buyback mechanics.
why_us: As AI agents start trading/moving funds, security gaps are critical. Early product signals with usage and integrations.
